title: Pool Operations Orchestra — Compact control slate for Dedicated GPU fleets
creator: Zoe Park
description:
Goal: Produce a compact, operator-focused control slate ("Orchestra") for Dedicated GPU pools that consolidates health signals, policy controls (autoscale & burst), quick cost impact previews, and safe rollout actions into a single horizontally-scannable surface. The slate is intended for SREs and platform engineers who need to triage pool health, apply temporary burst capacity, tune autoscale policies, and preview cost/latency trade-offs before committing changes.

Background: Current pool management surfaces are fragmented — health metrics live in a separate dashboard, autoscale config is buried in a modal, and cost previews are not available when changing policies. This increases context switching during incidents and slows operational response. The "Orchestra" slate aims to reduce mean time to resolution and lower the risk of policy misconfiguration by making key controls visible and reversible from one place.

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma mockups for desktop and tablet of the Orchestra slate (overview row + expanded policy drawer)
- Interactive prototype demonstrating: simulated load slider, burst toggle with credit preview, autoscale rule quick-edit, and cost delta preview modal
- A design spec (Confluence) with accessibility notes, microcopy, and error states for rollbacks/fallbacks
- Hand-off assets and annotated component list for frontend/engineering
acceptance_criteria: Overview row displays 90d sparkline, current capacity, queue depth, and a single- glance health indicator
Burst control allows setting duration (minutes) and GPU count with live cost preview before apply
Autoscale quick-edit supports: target utilization, min/max nodes, cooldown windows, and a performance impact tooltip
Simulated load slider shows projected latency and token-cost delta for given policy changes
Every change path includes a confirm step that shows expected cost delta and an immediate rollback entry in the audit log
Design implements keyboard-focused navigation and meets WCAG contrast for key elements
comments: 2025-11-14 — Initial discovery with ENG: identified missing cost preview in existing flow; Eng requested 'simulated load' to validate QoS impact
2025-11-20 — First wireframes reviewed by PM (Aisha Khan) — PM asked to surface SLA tiers per pool and to include 'safety caps' for burst by default
2025-11-25 — Design sync with Research: validated that SREs prefer a horizontal 'conductor' row for quick scan, suggested motion pattern for expanding policy drawer
2025-11-28 — Prototype v0 posted in Figma; requested: clearer failure state for failed burst (auto-fallback to lower tier) and add toast-level feedback after policy apply

2025-12-01 — Design review with Eng (Miguel Ortega) — agreed on API hooks required: cost_preview(api), simulate_load(api), apply_policy(api). Engineering requested an optional 'dry-run' apply endpoint to validate rollout before mutation
2025-12-01 — UX review notes: reduce cognitive load by collapsing less-frequently-used metrics into a secondary drawer; add confirmation microcopy to avoid accidental bursts
